correctness.rationale: On the all-edges-hit event, convexity gives a retained segment on every original side and a chord between the two nearest samples across each vertex. For a side with one sample the retained segment has length zero. The cosine rule gives the stated expression with the interior angle, and homogeneity gives exactly the N/L scaling. Define an endpoint gap on a missed side to be its full length. At fixed rescaled thresholds the forbidden intervals eventually fit disjointly inside the half-edges, so their joint avoidance probability is (1−sum(s_i)/N)^N, proving joint convergence to 2m independent unit exponentials. Each scaled capped gap has an exponential tail bound. On the exceptional event the deficit is bounded by L by perimeter monotonicity (also for a segment), and the exceptional probability decays exponentially; consequently all fixed moments are uniformly integrable. For two unit exponentials their sum is Gamma(shape 2, rate 1), independent of their uniform fraction. Conditioning gives the displayed Laplace factor. With a=cos(α/2), b=sin(α/2), the square-root integral is the integral of sqrt(b²+a²z²) on [0,1]; the primitive gives 1/2+(b²/2a)log cot(α/4). Expanding the square of c gives integral c²=μ−(1+cos α)/3. These yield the stated mean and variance, and the chord increases strictly with the angle for positive gaps.
residual_risks: The empty-edge cap makes the gap variables well defined off the good event; the convention cannot affect the limit in law or moments.

The checker is numerical and not a proof. It attempts 70 hull draws per polygon and skips empty-edge draws, and its five-angle loop performs 15 Laplace evaluations rather than the nine stated in VERIFICATION.md. Neither affects the analytic theorem.

residual_risks: This assesses mathematical value added over the inspected exact coverage, not historical priority or the usefulness of the law itself.
